text:
Samir: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak we rolled 3h ago, APAC prefix cache hit-rate tanked. p50 token latency +12ms, p95 +40ms on small requests. Hit-rate went from ~68% to ~42% for short prompts. Anyone else seeing this?
Lina: Oof. I saw increased misses too. Can you paste the per-region breakdown?
Samir: sure, quick snapshot (1m window):
EU: hit 71% -> 70%
US: hit 69% -> 66%
APAC: hit 68% -> 42%
Overall tok/sec same but miss->cold path increased apac latency a lot.
Aj: Did the kernel selector change modify any tokenization/normalization code? Cache keys should be independent of kernel but small differences can leak in. :thinking_face: 
Samir: I dug a bit. The runtime change introduced a small pre-tokenization whitespace normalization in the new kernel path (to optimize attention stride). Most requests are unaffected, but prefixes with trailing newlines/spaces now normalize differently, producing different cache keys. Example: 
```
# old key generation
key = prefix.strip().lower()
# new path (accidental)
key = normalize_whitespace(prefix)  # collapses "
" differently
```
Lina: That would create misses when one region is still on the old runtime and another picks the new kernel. Do we have mixed-version rollout in APAC?
Maria: Yes — Dedicated node pool in apac was on the canary image. Replication lag for KV apply spiked during the deploy window too. replication_apply_ms median: EU 48ms, US 60ms, APAC 1200ms (tail >> 2s). Combined that's likely causing coherence gaps.
Aj: So two factors: key normalization drift + replication lag -> cold misses amplified in APAC. Behavior fits.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-16T10:22:10Z started: runtime-selector:v2.14 -> v2.15 (canary apac).
Samir: I ran a targeted compare on a few prefixes and confirmed different normalized strings on v2.14 vs v2.15. Misses map to the new normalized forms.
Lina: Short-term mitigation: route APAC traffic to EU warm pool for prefix-serving while we backfill APAC cache. Maybe add a warm-first routing override (prefer warm cache copy even if higher latency).
Aj: Agreed. Proposed routing tweak: prefer region with warm_cache_score >= 0.8, else use latency-first. Quick config diff: 
```yaml
routing:
  policy: >
    - if warm_cache_score >= 0.8 then prefer_region(warmness)
    - else prefer_region(latency)
```
Maria: Also we should stop the canary in APAC until we fix normalization and replication. I can flip the canary to EU-only.
Samir: Action list I ran locally: 1) rollback kernel-normalization in selector branch (PR #4512), 2) start APAC cache priming job (sample 200k prefixes) to backfill, 3) add routing warm-first temporary rule, 4) triage replication throttle. Results: priming job warmed ~55% of cold keys within 15m for sampled set. p95 in APAC dropped ~20% after priming.
Lina: Can you share the priming job command? I'll spin it up on staging and then prod.
Samir: Command snippet I used: 
```bash
# sample prefixes from recent traffic and write to priming queue
python tools/priming.py --src recent-prefix-samples.json --region apac --concurrency 40 --target 200000
```
Aj: For longer term: ensure cache key normalization is centralized and run CI fuzz tests that compare normalized keys across kernels (v2 selector matrix). Also add a small E2E test that simulates mixed-version routing.
Maria: I'm increasing replication workers in APAC temporarily and monitoring apply latency. If replication_apply_ms tail drops under 500ms and priming completes, we can remove the warm-first routing.
Samir: I'll keep the revert PR ready but not merge until we confirm replication. If we want to keep the normalization change, we need a one-time rekey / migration so all regions share canonical keys. That is heavier: requires coordinated backfill migration job.
Lina: For immediate cadence: Maria to scale replication (in progress), Aj to patch routing policy (10m), Samir to run prod priming (in progress), I will run cross-version key normalization tests and open a migration plan doc if we keep the behavior change.
deploy-bot: Deployment paused in apac per manual override by Maria.
Samir: Thanks all. I'll post a follow-up with numbers in 30m. If anyone sees new regressions, @Samir please ping. :thumbsup:
